newsitem.title: USA: S&P may raise Tyco International ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P may raise Tyco International ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said it placed its ratings of Tyco International Ltd on CreditWatch with positive implications following the announcement that Tyco has agreed to acquire ADT Ltd, parent of ADT Operations Inc in a stock for stock transaction valued at $5.6 billion.
Ratings of ADT Operations Inc remain on CreditWatch with positive implications, S&P said.
S&P announced the rating action on Monday.

The combined companies will have a more favorable business risk profile than either company on its own. ADT's strong position in electronic security services is expected to complement Tyco's industrial and commercial fire protection operations, adding a less cyclical service business with a high level of recurring sales to Tyco's diversified portfolio.
ADT gains a solid platform for growth as part of a successful, diversified conglomerate.

The financial profile is expected to be strong initially, reflecting Tyco's recent equity offering, potential for conversion into equity of convertible debt securities at ADT, and possible excercise of warrants.

Total debt to capital is expected to be in the low 30 percent area following the acquisition and the above items, net of acquisition-related restructuring charges of about $650 million (of which about $300 million will be cash charges).
Any rating action will be dependent on the outcome of a full review of the combined entity's business position and financial policies.
RATINGS PLACED ON CREDITWATCH WITH POSITIVE IMPLICATIONS
RATING REMAINING ON CREDITWATCH WITH POSITIVE IMPLICATIONS
$250 million 8.25 percent senior notes due August 1, 2000
$350 million sub notes due 2003 (gtd by ADT) BB-plus
$776.3 million zero coupon conv sub notes due 2010 BB-plus
